Article Title: Army soldier found hanging in a shed in Jammu; probe on
Article Text:
Soldier found dead at Jammu Army camp

NEW DELHI: A 45-year-old Army soldier was found hanging in a shed at the Sunjwan camp in Jammu on Sunday, news agency PTI reported citing officials.The deceased was identified as Naik Wagh Ambades, a resident of Maharashtra. Officials said he allegedly died by suicide.The reason behind the alleged suicide was not immediately known. Police have initiated inquest proceedings to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the death.His body was taken to Government Medical College Hospital in Jammu for postmortem and other legal procedures.
Article Summary: Soldier found hanging in a shed at the Sunjwan camp in Jammu on Sunday. Naik Wagh Ambades, a resident of Maharashtra, allegedly died by suicide. Police have initiated inquest proceedings to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the death.

Article Title: Punjab arms network busted: AK-47, grenades seized, accused linked to foreign smugglers
Article Text:
Image source: DGP Punjab Polic X account

NEW DELHI: Amritsar Rural Police have busted an illegal arms and explosives supply network, arresting one accused.In a post shared by the DGP Punjab Police on X, the police said the operation also resulted in the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, a magazine, live cartridges and two hand grenades.Preliminary investigation has revealed that the accused is allegedly linked to foreign-based smugglers and was involved in procuring illegal weapons, police said.An FIR has been registered at Gharinda police station in Amritsar under relevant sections of the Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.Further investigation is underway to uncover the wider network and establish its backward and forward linkages, police said.The Punjab Police said it remained committed to maintaining strict vigil against illegal arms trafficking and organised criminal networks and taking firm action against those involved in the illegal supply chain.
Article Summary: Amritsar Rural Police have busted an illegal arms and explosives supply network. The operation also resulted in the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, a magazine, live cartridges and two hand grenades. The accused is allegedly linked to foreign- based smugglers and was involved in procuring illegal weapons.

Article Title: ‘She will continue’: Thiruvananthapuram mayor denies BJP councillor Sreelekha resigned from post
Article Text:
Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from Sreelekha on September 30.

Mayor says Sreelekha will remain councillor

CPM attacks BJP councillor

Sreelekha's role in BJP

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V V Rajesh on Sunday said former Kerala DGP and BJP councillor R Sreelekha would continue in office, denying that she had resigned from the Corporation.The controversy began after a message purportedly posted by Sreelekha in a WhatsApp group of residents in her ward said she had submitted her resignation to the Mayor and would give a copy to the District Collector on October 5.Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from Sreelekha on September 30 but had not sent it to the Corporation Secretary, who is authorised to accept such resignations. He had also said the letter cited personal difficulties.On Sunday, however, Rajesh said there was no resignation letter."Who told you that she has given the resignation letter? She will continue and I have said it yesterday itself," he said.When asked about the WhatsApp message attributed to Sreelekha, Rajesh did not directly address it. He instead said there was no threat to the functioning of the Corporation."You want the governance to take place smoothly. As all desire, the governance will go forward strongly," he said.Rajesh said councillors often submit letters seeking funds for their wards or raising issues related to their functioning."Such a letter was given to me for the smooth operations in the ward. As she is a ruling councillor, I find that some of the matters cited in it require the party's intervention. Some have to be done by the Mayor. We will address the matters as in letters given by other councillors," he said.He said Sreelekha would remain a councillor and complete her five-year term.Sreelekha has not yet publicly responded to the conflicting statements over her alleged resignation.CPM leader and former minister V Sivankutty criticised Sreelekha and questioned her credibility."Nothing that Sreelekha says can be believed. Not only that, she will resort to any threat to secure position and power. This should only be viewed as a threat directed at the BJP to gain new positions," he said.Asked whether Sreelekha was putting pressure on the BJP with a possible move towards the Congress, Sivankutty said some politicians would move wherever they saw greater benefits."Naturally, some go where there is greater benefit. They will move to wherever they get the maximum advantage," he said.The BJP took control of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation for the first time last year after securing the support of 51 councillors, including an Independent, in the 101-member civic body.Sreelekha was elected from the Sasthamangalam ward on a BJP ticket in last year's local body elections. She is currently the BJP's state vice president.Her continuation as a BJP councillor is significant for the party because its majority in the Corporation is narrow and depends on the support of an Independent councillor.Sreelekha also contested the Vattiyoorkavu Assembly seat in April but lost to Congress leader K Muraleedharan.
Article Summary: Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V V Rajesh on Sunday said former Kerala DGP and BJP councillor R Sreelekha would continue in office. He denied that she had resigned from the Corporation. Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from SreeLekha on September 30. He had also said the letter cited personal difficulties.

Article Title: CJP protest: Scuffle breaks out near Shiv Sena Bhavan as supporters return from stir; watch
Article Text:
A scuffle erupted near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after a protest





MUMBAI: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) returned from a protest at Shivaji Park.A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other.The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.The incident followed a CJP protest at Shivaji Park over the party’s demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Before the protest, a Dadar resident had opposed the demonstration. “They are doing it forcefully. This protest should not take place,” the resident said, adding that such demonstrations disturb peace in the area.The CJP has been demanding Kumar’s resignation and changes to the functioning and appointment process of the Election Commission. The Election Commission currently lists Gyanesh Kumar as the Chief Election Commissioner.Mumbai Police had earlier denied permission for the CJP to hold its October 2 protest at Shivaji Park. The party later announced a “Jail Bharo Andolan”.Meanwhile, a 75-year-old Thane resident died after suffering a heart attack while attending the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Friday evening.The deceased was identified as Gopalakrishna Subbaiya Pillai, a resident of Dosti West County in Thane.Pillai arrived at Shivaji Park around 4.30pm to attend the protest. Around 5pm, he complained of chest pain. His friend and police personnel at the spot helped take him to Sushrusha Hospital in Shivaji Park.Police personnel tried to revive him with CPR before he was taken to the hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment. Police said doctors attributed his death to a heart attack.
Article Summary: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party returned from a protest at Shivaji Park. A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other. The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.

Article Title: Flydubai attack: Co-pilot identified as Hamam Alhamami was barred from flying in Oman over 'extremist views'
Article Text:
As per reports, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. His alleged views are being examined as part of a wider investigation into possible Islamic radicalisation and terrorist motives

Removed from Oman Air training role

Pro-Palestinian material found among belongings

Questions over clearance for Tel Aviv flight

Who is Hamam Alhamami?

What happened aboard flydubai flight

The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv has been identified as Hamam Alhamami. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views.Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reported that he had spent much of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria, where he was allegedly influenced by extremist ideas before travelling to the UAE.The revelations follow a CNN report that Alhamami had been removed from a training role at Oman Air, Oman's national carrier, last year. However, he was later given another role at the airline, the report said, citing a regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter.Further reports have raised questions about Alhamami's alleged ideological views. i24 News, citing an Emirati source, reported that leaflets and publications from “Free Palestine” groups, along with other pro-Palestinian material, were found among his belongings.According to the report, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. The report said investigators were examining the material as part of a broader probe into his alleged Islamic radicalisation and possible terrorist motives.The reports have also raised questions about how Alhamami was cleared to serve on a Tel Aviv-bound flight despite being an Omani citizen. Oman does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.An Israeli official told CNN that several agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry, were investigating how Alhamami came to be part of the flight crew.According to the report, Alhamami is an Omani citizen. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and spent several years of his life in the UAE. The Jerusalem Post, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that he did not hold a second nationality.CNN reported that Alhamami had worked for flydubai for only eight months. He had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco's national carrier.Alhamami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk. He is facing a terrorism investigation in the UAE.The September 30 incident took place aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Alhamami allegedly attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit in what is being investigated as a possible terror-driven attempt to bring down the aircraft.The confrontation triggered a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping approximately 16,000 feet within two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was transmitted.Despite suffering severe injuries, Captain Machchhar resisted the attack and managed to open the cockpit door. Flight crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit and restrained Alhamami, allowing the crew to regain control of the aircraft.Two non-duty aviators who were travelling aboard the flight also helped assume control of the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all 180 occupants disembarking safely.
Article Summary: Hamam Alhamami is the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views. Pro-Palestinian material was found among his belongings, according to reports.

Article Title: Of 97 left out in Goa, 88 are back, 3 others are Portuguese citizens: EC
Article Text:
Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The office of the Goa chief electoral officer on Thursday said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. However, he also revealed that three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India."In respect of voters who are currently residing outside India, officials are making efforts to establish and maintain contact with them for necessary action," the CEO said while sharing the status report on the 97 cases on X.Section 9 of the Constitution disallows dual citizenship. Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents. Portugal recognises dual citizenship; however, since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.As per Sec 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person's Indian citizenship automatically ceases upon acquiring foreign citizenship.Thus, three of the Portuguese passport holders in Goa may be classified as non-citizens, making them ineligible to be enrolled as Indian electors, said a source.Incidentally, Portuguese passport holders form 3% of the cohort of 97 electors for which the Goa CEO had repeatedly written to the EC after the ERO could not add them back via ERONet, leading the ECs to also raise questions on why access for such changes was 'centralised' and not available to the field officers. The issue was further amplified by the opposition parties after The Indian Express reported on the alleged internal notes of the election commissioners in this regard.EC sources on Thursday said the due diligence by the ERO the second time around may have served the purpose of SIR, as it is aimed at eliminating ineligible persons from the voters' list. Also, the fact that the issue was detected at the ERO level proves that the absolute right to add or delete a voter, based on verification, remains with the field officers, an EC officer told TOI.
Article Summary: 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. Three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India. Since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.

Article Title: 'AAP asked you not to': Congress leader claims CJP refused party's help during Assam detention
Article Text:
Congress, CJP spar over Assam outreach

'You asked us to stay out of it'

'Sidelined Neha Bora'

Row follows Ranka's criticism

NEW DELHI: Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh has claimed that Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka refused to meet Congress leaders during his recent Assam visit. He alleged that the group was told to stay away because its outreach was "an Aam Aadmi Party initiative".Singh's response came after Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das called out a fake "liberal ecosystem", saying that they believed they were alone responsible for “saving India, saving constitution”. However, they did not name Congress directly.Singh made the allegation in a post on X on Saturday while responding to Ranka, who had criticised what he described as an “entire ‘self-declared liberal’ ecosystem” targeting CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.Singh said Congress workers had helped CJP members after they were detained by Assam Police and claimed that Ranka nevertheless declined a courtesy meeting with Congress leaders, including Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi.This comes days after Ranka and more than 40 CJP volunteers were detained in Guwahati ahead of a regional volunteers' meeting. Opposition parties, including Congress, AAP, the Assam Jatiya Parishad and Raijor Dal, had criticised the police action.Addressing Ranka, Singh said Congress members had helped secure the release of CJP workers after their detention.“When you were detained by Assam Police. We, Congress people helped to get CJP people out. Yet you categorically refused to have even a courtesy meeting with our Congress leaders and Gaurav Sir,” Singh said."You refused it because the Aam Aadmi Party asked you to not to. Kunki Chowdhury who was your Host in Guwahati, was on Election Campaign with AJP President Lurin Gogoi Da for a Congress Candidate in Nagaon. Even they had asked you to meet and discuss with Congress. Yet not once, you chose to engage with Congress or our students wing. You asked us to stay out of it. And that it is a Aam Aadmi Party initiative," he added.Singh also referred to Kunki Chowdhury, at whose residence Ranka and other CJP members were reportedly detained. He claimed Chowdhury had asked Ranka to meet Congress leaders and discuss the group's activities.CJP members had been detained from the residence of Assam Jatiya Parishad leader Kunki Chowdhury in the Dispur area ahead of their scheduled meeting.Singh further accused Ranka and CJP of trying to portray the movement as an AAP initiative and referred to the group's earlier protests in Delhi.“We know how you sidelined Neha Bora in the Jantar Mantar 1.0 protests and when even Left chose to engage with our Leader Rahul Gandhi Ji. You decided you will not engage under direct instructions of Arvind Kejriwal,” he said.He also alleged that AAP had previously sought to associate itself with movements led by others, citing the India Against Corruption movement and activist Sonam Wangchuk's protest.“Aam Aadmi Party is known for piggy riding and hijacking issues of others,” Singh said.Singh said CJP was “a people's movement” and argued that it should not be treated as the property of any political party.“Let us keep it civil and issue centric. The cause is bigger than a political party,” he said.“CJP is a decentralised movement. There is no one Supreme Leader or his hierarchy. We all are equals. That is why people support it.”Ranka's post that triggered Singh's response had accused a “self-declared liberal” group of targeting Dipke and questioning his growing reach.“An entire “self-declared liberal” ecosystem has been activated to denounce @abhijeet_dipke and the fact that he has been able to capture the imagination of millions of Indians after a LONG LONG time,” Ranka said.CJP co-convenor Saurav Das also criticised what he described as a group from outside the BJP that believed it alone was responsible for “saving India, saving constitution”. Neither Ranka nor Das named a political party in their posts."It’s a very big problem. A certain section—not just the BJP—another party thinks “saving India, saving constitution” is only their job. They are self-declared liberals and self-declared thekedars of the constitution," he said."It’s a very salty ecosystem, acting worse than the BJP’s ecosystem sometimes. They must realise that they can’t divide and rule through such tactics. Their massive failures over the years has led us to this moment where the young have to show the way. So they should just zip it on us and focus on how to support the young! Total buffoons!" he added.The latest exchange has brought CJP's political affiliations and its relationship with opposition parties into focus, even as the organisation continues its outreach on issues including education and electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh claims Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co- convenor Ashutosh Ranka refused to meet Congress leaders during his recent Assam visit. He alleged that the group was told to stay away because its outreach was "an Aam Aadmi Party initiative"

Article Title: Watch: Netanyahu invites PM Modi, pilot Smit Machchhar to Israel I-Day event
Article Text:
Netanyahu praised the pilot for his actions during the incident and hailed him as 'hero of the entire world'.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with crash axe

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day event. Speaking to Machchhar, he called him a "hero" of Israel, India and the entire world for foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight.Netanyahu spoke to the 38-year-old pilot on Saturday while Machchhar was undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. During the emotional conversation, Machchhar recounted how he was attacked by his co-pilot inside the cockpit and revealed new details about the incident."It's our highest honour that we give on our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens, but I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will embrace you. They do now, and they will then too. So we hope to see you very soon in Israel," Netanyahu told Machchhar.The Israeli Prime Minister's office later said on X, "You are a hero for Israel, India, and the entire world. I invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi and you to light a flame on Israeli Independence Day.""During the emotional conversation that took place this evening, the Prime Minister asked Captain Machchhar how it all started, and Machchhar revealed new details about the terrifying moments in the cockpit," the post said.Machchhar told Netanyahu that the co-pilot had wanted to pray before the attack. He said he looked towards the front of the cockpit out of respect while the co-pilot prayed."...while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back, and suddenly, after, I would say about four-five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head."My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something was not right. But then after that, the blows kept coming one after the other, and that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," Machchhar said.Netanyahu praised the pilot for his actions during the incident."You saved so many souls. I think you saved something bigger. You saved the spirit of the world...It's something that is being justly hailed around the world. You're a hero of Israel. You're a hero of India. You're a hero of the entire world," Netanyahu told Machchhar."You know, I guess it's a twist of fate, and a twist of faith, and what you did is remarkable. I heard, of course, from the Israeli passengers what transpired after that, and you're a great hero, and you were accompanied by heroes, and you saved the day," he said.Netanyahu also told Machchhar he was "amazed at his courage" and "at your coolness of judgment under impossible conditions."The incident took place on Wednesday aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying 174 passengers to Israel. Machchhar was allegedly attacked by his co-pilot with a crash axe, an emergency tool kept inside the cockpit.The aircraft transmitted emergency signals and made a rapid descent of more than 17,000 feet, from 34,000 feet. It eventually made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The descent was so extreme that part of the aircraft's rudder was reportedly torn away.The co-pilot has been identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the matter.Machchhar received initial treatment in Tabuk before being shifted to Abu Dhabi for continued medical care.The co-pilot of a Flydubai flight, Hamam al-Hammami, allegedly attacked the captain with a crash axe inside the cockpit and attempted to take control of the aircraft. UAE described the incident as a terrorist attack.UAE prosecutor general Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said the co-pilot launched the attack during Wednesday's flight and tried to seize control of the aircraft. The incident was subsequently classified by UAE authorities as an attempted terrorist attack.
Article Summary: Netanyahu spoke to the 38-year-old pilot on Saturday while Machchhar was undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. He called him a "hero" of Israel, India and the entire world for foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel- bound flydubai flight. Israeli Prime Minister's office later said, "I invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi and you to light a flame on Israeli Independence Day"

Article Title: Kerala orders vigilance probe into 2006 suicide case linked to CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
2006 suicide case naming Gyanesh Kumar triggers Kerala vigilance probe

NEW DELHI: Kerala home minister Ramesh Chennithala has ordered a Vigilance investigation into allegations of irregularities involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar during his tenure as the state’s Public Works Department Secretary in 2006, news agency ANI reported.The case concerns the death by suicide of Malaysian civil engineer Lee See Been, who was associated with the PATI-BEL consortium involved in the upgradation of MC Road under the Kerala State Transport Project. Been’s suicide note reportedly mentioned Gyanesh Kumar.The investigation has been ordered following allegations that external pressure was exerted and that the original inquiry into the case was derailed.Chennithala has directly instructed the Vigilance Director to conduct a thorough inquiry into the allegations of external influence in the case involving Gyanesh Kumar and take appropriate action based on the findings, the Home Minister’s Office said."Yesterday, Malayinkeezhu Venugopal, a Congress activist, gave me a petition regarding the malpractices and corrupt activities of Gyanesh Kumar when he was PWD secretary in Keralam...The representation reveals some of the serious issues. Also, in between, my Malaysian project engineer, Lee, committed suicide. In the suicide note, it has been mentioned about PWD Secretary Gyanesh Kumar very clearly. So the government cannot sit idle. I cannot become a mute spectator... I had forwarded it to the vigilance director to go into the details of the petition and take legal action to deliver justice," Chennithala said.Official sources said the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) will conduct a probe into the allegations, as cited by news agency PTI.The development comes as opposition parties, student organisations and youth groups held protests in Delhi and Mumbai on Friday, demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and claims of mass voter deletions.Around 700 people were detained in Delhi, while thousands gathered at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park despite police denying permission for the demonstrations.In Delhi, those detained included AAP leaders Atishi, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Sanjeev Jha, AISA president Neha Bora, CPI(M) leaders M A Baby and Brinda Karat, CPI national secretary P Sandosh Kumar, RJD leader Manoj Jha, social activist Yogendra Yadav, DYFI president A A Rahim and former JNUSU president Aishe Ghosh.The agitation intensified after media reports claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months regarding decisions and procedures linked to the SIR exercise and other electoral matters.The reported objections covered issues including voter deletions, Form 6 and access to electoral-roll databases. The Election Commission, however, rejected suggestions that the objections reflected institutional dissent, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its routine administrative and decision-making process.The ECI said the three-member commission had taken all decisions, including those related to the SIR, unanimously.
Article Summary: Kerala home minister Ramesh Chennithala orders investigation into allegations of irregularities involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Case concerns death by suicide of Malaysian civil engineer Lee See Been, who was associated with the PATI-BEL consortium. Been’s suicide note reportedly mentioned Kumar.

Article Title: ‘Gyanesh ka resignation to lekar rahenge’: Congress calls for fresh protest in Delhi
Article Text:
‘Gyanesh ka resignation to lekar rahenge’: Congress steps up protest against CEC Kumar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Sunday announced a protest in Delhi calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In a post on X, the party said its supporters would gather at India Gate at 5 pm before marching to Jantar Mantar.“Koi kitna bhi zor laga le.. Gyanesh ka Resignation to lekar rahenge. Chaliye, Sham ko milte hain. 4th October. 5 PM onwards. India Gate to Jantar Mantar,” the post read.Earlier on Saturday, nearly 200 protesters were detained in connection with demonstrations at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, officials said. Delhi Police also registered cases over Friday’s protest under provisions related to disobedience of orders and obstruction and assault of public servants.On Saturday, protesters marched from Patel Chowk towards Jantar Mantar, where police and paramilitary personnel had erected barricades and deployed additional forces to prevent them from reaching the designated protest area.Police invoked Sections 223(a), 221, 132 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) in connection with Friday’s protests. The provisions relate to disobedience of a lawful order issued by a public servant, obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions, assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from performing his duty, and acts carried out by several persons in furtherance of a common intention, respectively.The All India Students’ Association (AISA) had called for fresh mobilisation on Saturday, a day after nearly 1,000 people were detained during protests in and around Jantar Mantar. Many of those detained on Friday were later released.AAP’s student wing, the Association of Students for Alternative Politics (ASAP), also staged a protest on Saturday. The organisation alleged that some of its volunteers were detained and taken to different parts of Delhi in a bus for several hours before being brought to Jafarpur police station.AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj questioned the continued detention of the student volunteers. Delhi Police did not immediately respond to the allegations.The latest action came a day after Delhi Police registered at least three FIRs in connection with Friday’s protests. Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station under Section 223 of the BNS for alleged disobedience of an order issued by a public servant.Ahead of Friday’s protest, police had imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) across the New Delhi district. The order prohibits gatherings of five or more people, processions, demonstrations, picketing, dharnas and slogan shouting without prior written permission.Around 5,000 police and paramilitary personnel, including more than 10 companies of paramilitary forces, were deployed across central Delhi on Friday. Barricades were erected at several locations, while drones were used to monitor crowded areas.Officials said police had received inputs that around 4,000 to 5,000 people could gather for the protest.The protests have also taken place amid a political debate over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The Election Commission has maintained that differences of opinion within the poll panel are part of institutional deliberations and that its orders follow established statutory procedures.
Article Summary: The Congress on Sunday announced a protest in Delhi calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In a post on X, the party said its supporters would gather at India Gate at 5 pm before marching to Jantar Mantar. The latest action came a day after Delhi Police registered at least three FIRs in connection with Friday's protests.

Article Title: Kashmir professor removed for ‘harassing’ students

Article Title: Drug addicts turn to painkillers amid Nasha Mukt crackdown in J&K
Article Text:
(Representative image): Investigations have so far led to the recovery of 2,19,425 tablets and capsules of pharmaceutical drugs, as well as 3.830 kg of codeine-containing liquid, including the storage containers, police said.

SRINAGAR: Drug users and peddlers in Jammu & Kashmir are increasingly turning to pharmaceutical opioids, primarily painkillers, amid an intensified crackdown under Nasha Mukt Abhiyaan to make the UT “narcotics-free”.“It seems they were mixing several painkiller drugs to get the effect of heroin,” a police officer said, adding that abusers frequently use prescription medicines like Tramadol and Tapentadol, which they refer to as “Tapal“ in their local slang.Investigations have so far led to the recovery of 2,19,425 tablets and capsules of pharmaceutical drugs, as well as 3.830 kg of codeine-containing liquid, including the storage containers, police said.Since its launch on April 11, Nasha Mukt Abhiyaan has resulted in over 4,000 arrests, the seizure of 288 properties, and registration of 3,257 cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. The campaign includes awareness programmes, the destruction of illicit poppy crops, and random urine drug testing for drivers.On Thursday, Srinagar police arrested eight people after busting a major network involved in the procurement, transportation, storage, distribution, and financing of banned pharmaceutical products, with supply lines extending well beyond J&K.Among those arrested was Haris Hameed Malla, a Srinagar resident identified as a key accused in the network allegedly headed by Waseem Ahmad Zargar. While Zargar claimed to operate a legitimate pharmaceutical business, Malla allegedly projected himself as an influential figure, frequently flaunting photographs with top police and civil officials.His Instagram account featured photographs with Union ministers Nitin Gadkari and Chirag Paswan, as well as Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and National Conference MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi. On his social media profiles, Malla described himself as the editor-in-chief of the “India News Panel” and a community journalist. Malla had also posted a letter on X, purportedly written by L-G Manoj Sinha, regarding the UT’s efforts to combat drug abuse.A police officer said Zargar, the alleged primary supplier, revealed details of the operation during questioning. Malla subsequently fled the Valley but was traced to Bengaluru, where he was arrested.As part of the ongoing case, a house and two vehicles were attached in Srinagar’s Old City. Officials noted that the case is highly significant as locals are increasingly coming forward to report the growing drug menace. In Maharaj Gunj subdivision of Old City alone, 34 houses have been attached over the past few years.
Article Summary: Drug users and peddlers in Jammu & Kashmir are increasingly turning to pharmaceutical opioids, primarily painkillers. The crackdown under Nasha Mukt Abhiyaan has resulted in over 4,000 arrests, the seizure of 288 properties, and registration of 3,257 cases.

JAMMU: A 19-year-old woman from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) was intercepted by Army personnel after she crossed the LoC in J&K’s Rajouri district, officials said Saturday.Nothing incriminating was found with Samiya Azeem when she was caught late Friday, the officials said, adding she is a resident of PoK’s Kotli district. “During preliminary interrogation, the girl maintained she had inadvertently crossed the LoC and entered Indian territory,” an official said.Troops found Samiya in the border village of Pukherni in Rajouri’s Nowshera sector. The teenager was later handed over to J&K Police officers for further detention and inquiries, the officials said.Inadvertent LoC crossings are not rare in J&K. Such intruders are often intercepted by Army troopers and handed over to local cops for identity verification before being repatriated through designated checkpoints following special flag meetings with Pakistani counterparts.On Sept 7 this year, Nazir Sadhir, a resident of Luni Pundra village in Pakistan’s Sialkot, was caught after inadvertently crossing the LoC.Checks followed, and he was later handed over to Pakistani Rangers by BSF personnel at Golpattan outpost.On June 9 this year, Javed Ali, a 14-year-old from PoK, was detained on this side of the LoC. He was handed over to Pakistan Army personnel a week later at Chakan Da Bagh border post after checks and other formalities.Abdul Hussain, a 70-year-old from Lehari Khurd village in Pakistan, was intercepted in Indian territory on March 25 this year and sent back within six hours after it was established that he had entered inadvertently.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday briefed a parliamentary consultative committee on India's "multifaceted" engagement with Russia, covering bilateral trade, investment and energy cooperation as well as New Delhi's diplomatic efforts to contribute towards ending the Ukraine conflict.Chairing the meeting on India-Russia relations, Jaishankar also informed members that Russia has agreed to take around 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, particularly in construction and logistics, people familiar with the discussions said, according to news agency PTI.Jaishankar said India and Russia share an ambition to expand bilateral trade in a more balanced manner, including by increasing Indian exports to Russia across seven sectors — automobiles, pharmaceuticals, food, marine products, engineering goods, chemicals and textiles.The minister highlighted various areas of bilateral engagement, including trade, investments, energy, connectivity, culture and people-to-people ties, according to a social media post by Jaishankar.The discussions also covered an India-Eurasian Economic Union Free Trade Agreement, the Chennai-Vladivostok corridor, the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) and the Northern Sea Route.On energy cooperation, Jaishankar said India's priority was to safeguard the interests of Indian consumers."Our approach is to maintain multiple sources of supply," he said, according to people familiar with the meeting.The government has also been seeking to expand opportunities for Indian workers in Russia.The Ukraine conflict also featured prominently in the discussions, with Jaishankar apprising the panel of India's position and recent diplomatic efforts to support dialogue and diplomacy.In his social media post, Jaishankar said he highlighted India's "active support to dialogue & diplomacy to end the Ukraine conflict".The minister referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's August 31 meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, where the PM said that "endless war must now give way to end of war".Jaishankar travelled to Ukraine last month and subsequently met the foreign ministers of Ukraine and Russia in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. During those engagements, he conveyed India's readiness to assist efforts to bring the conflict to an end, people familiar with the meeting said."If India can be of any help in any manner to bring the war to an end, it is ready to do so," Jaishankar said in his conversations.Putin's recent remarks at the Valdai Club in Moscow were also discussed. He had said Prime Minister Modi "has very good ideas for finding mutually acceptable solutions" to bring peace.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha's remarks appreciating India's efforts were also noted during the meeting.Jaishankar also briefed the committee on the government's efforts to secure the release of Indian nationals serving in the Russian military.The government has engaged with Russian authorities, including at the highest levels, for the early discharge of such individuals, the people cited above said.So far, around 140 Indian nationals have been discharged, while India is in touch with Russian authorities regarding the whereabouts of 55 Indian nationals who are reportedly working for the Russian Arm.The government has also been taking action against agents who recruit Indians for such roles, with members being briefed about the risks faced by Indian citizens joining the Russian Army.The parliamentary committee meeting thus covered India's economic and energy engagement with Russia alongside its diplomatic efforts on Ukraine and its continuing efforts to secure the release of Indian nationals serving in the Russian military.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar briefed a parliamentary consultative committee on India's "multifaceted" engagement with Russia. He highlighted bilateral trade, investment and energy cooperation as well as New Delhi's diplomatic efforts to contribute towards ending the Ukraine conflict. Russia has agreed to take around 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Saturday summoned the Chargé d'Affaires of the Pakistan high commission to lodge a strong protest over what it described as the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan.It also rejected as “baseless and motivated” Pakistan’s allegations over an October 2 incident in the Ferozepur sector of Punjab along the International Border.MEA said that Pakistan was informed that three individuals had entered Indian territory and continued moving towards the border fence despite repeated warnings from the BSF to return. Article Title: Delhi women’s safety protests: Shivraj Chouhan reacts to viral ‘kachori-samosa’ slogans

NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has reacted to viral videos from women-led protests in Delhi, questioning why women and girls have been forced to raise slogans about their safety and men. The remarks came amid demonstrations following the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old.Chouhan referred to one of the slogans doing the rounds online, “Ek kachori-do samosa, in mardo ka kya bharosa”, and said the situation required serious consideration.“Why has the situation come to this, that our daughters have to chant slogans like 'One kachori, two samosas'? We must think seriously about this,” he said in a post on X, sharing a video of himself at an event.The protests have also produced a series of rhyming slogans that have spread across social media, including, “Ek kachori, do samosa, in mardon ka kya bharosa,” “1 jeera, 2 ajwain, mard samaj do resign” and “Thandi chai garam karo, mard jaat sharam karo.”The slogans, which have circulated widely through Instagram, X and other platforms, have become part of the online vocabulary around the protests. The demonstrations were triggered by concerns over women’s safety following the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old at Aastha Kunj Park near Lady Shri Ram College.Chouhan called for a collective commitment to women’s safety and dignity.“We must take a resolve— We will respect our sisters and daughters, we will ensure their safety, and we will protect their rights,” he said.The first major demonstration was held on September 23, when around 200 students from Delhi University and affiliated institutions, including Lady Shri Ram College for Women, Miranda House, Gargi College and Dr BR Ambedkar University, took to the streets.On September 25, hundreds of women students marched near Delhi University’s South Campus, demanding safer public spaces and stronger action against sexual harassment. Another demonstration was later held at the Faculty of Arts.The protests have since been followed by measures from civic and security agencies. The Delhi Development Authority and Municipal Corporation of Delhi undertook safety audits of public parks, focusing on lighting, security personnel at entry and exit points and patrolling after sundown. Delhi Police also stepped up patrolling across parks and other areas.All three accused in the Aastha Kunj case have been arrested, according to PTI. One accused was pursuing a law course, whole another was arrested after an encounter with a Delhi Police.The issue has also drawn political reactions. Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi backed the student-led protests and said, “Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them. Across our country, women are afraid to walk the streets, afraid of being harassed, afraid of being raped. And the government’s answer: stay at home,” Gandhi said.Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal also questioned restrictions placed on women, while chief minister Rekha Gupta said women’s safety should not come at the cost of restricting their freedom.Gupta said the Delhi government was strengthening safety infrastructure, including 50,000 CCTV cameras and one lakh streetlights.
Article Summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan reacts to viral videos from women-led protests in Delhi. Chouhan questions why women and girls have been forced to raise slogans about their safety and men. Demonstrations triggered by concerns over women’s safety following alleged gang rape of 17-year-old.

NEW DELHI: CPI Rajya Sabha leader P Sandosh Kumar, who was detained during a protest at Jantar Mantar on Friday, has written to Union home minister Amit Shah seeking his intervention over alleged police violence, arbitrary detentions and the concealment of identification badges by Delhi Police personnel.The protest was held over concerns surrounding the functioning of the Election Commission of India, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, changes to Form-6 and the poll body's IT systems. Protesters had also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Kumar said he was among those detained along with workers and members of the CPI(M), CPI(ML)L, AAP, AISF, AIYF, SFI, DYFI, AISA and civil society groups.“I was myself detained yesterday along with workers of my party, the CPI(M), CPI(ML)L, AAP, cadres of the AISF, AIYF, SFI, DYFI, AISA and members of the civil society,” Kumar said in his letter.Kumar alleged that police had responded to peaceful protests with “violence, mass detentions, internet shutdowns and manhandling”, rather than facilitating the exercise of democratic rights.A key concern raised by the CPI leader was the alleged absence of visible name plates or identification badges on some police personnel involved in detentions and crowd-control measures.Referring to the Supreme Court's directions in the D K Basu vs State of West Bengal case, Kumar said police personnel carrying out arrests or handling detainees were required to bear “accurate, visible and clear identification and name tags with their designations”. He also cited Delhi Police Standing Order No 51, which prescribes visible name plates as part of the uniform.“This is not a minor procedural matter: identification is fundamental to accountability when the State exercises coercive power against citizens,” Kumar said.Kumar also referred to reports and visual material from an earlier protest on July 20, alleging that plain-clothes personnel and officers without visible identification badges had used force against protesters.“The fact that the same conduct was repeated on October 2 makes the matter serious,” he said.The CPI leader also sought an inquiry into the alleged use of facial-recognition technology at Jantar Mantar. He referred to an investigation which, he said, found discrepancies between people identified through the system as present at a student protest and records showing some of them were already in jail in connection with criminal cases.Kumar called for a time-bound inquiry into the use of force, alleged arbitrary detentions, concealment of identification badges, manhandling of protesters, deployment of plain-clothes personnel and use of facial-recognition systems.He urged Shah to direct that people exercising their right to peaceful protest be protected and that police personnel deployed for crowd-control and detention duties remain identifiable.“Democratic dissent cannot be met with methods reminiscent of the British Raj police,” Kumar said.“Delhi Police must understand that its duty is to protect citizens and facilitate their constitutional rights, not to intimidate, assault or silence them,” he added.
Article Summary: CPI Rajya Sabha leader P Sandosh Kumar was detained during a protest at Jantar Mantar on Friday. He has written to Union home minister Amit Shah seeking his intervention over alleged police violence, arbitrary detentions and the concealment of identification badges by Delhi Police personnel.

NEW DELHI: Retired DGP and Bharatiya Janata Party councillor R Sreelekha has reportedly resigned from the Thiruvananthapuram corporation amid reported dissatisfaction over not being made mayor, despite being projected as the party's candidate for the post during the 2025 local body elections.Thiruvananthapuram mayor VV Rajesh confirmed that he had received Sreelekha's resignation letter and said efforts were under way to resolve the issue amicably.Speaking to reporters, Rajesh said Sreelekha had cited personal inconveniences as the reason for her resignation."Personal inconveniences are natural. When working as public representatives, we often encounter inconveniences in many matters. Whatever can be resolved, we will resolve as we go," he said."On September 30, the resignation letter was submitted to me. The letter has to be given to the corporation secretary. Based on the letter I received and the information shared with me, I am making efforts to resolve the matter amicably and move forward in whatever way possible," he added.The resignation came to light after a message purportedly posted by Sreelekha in a WhatsApp group of residents of her ward said she had submitted her resignation to the mayor and would hand over a copy to the district collector on October 5.In the message, she thanked residents for their cooperation.Meanwhile, Thiruvananthapuram Corporation secretary J Muhammed Shafi said the resignation letter submitted by Sreelekha to the mayor was not valid, as only he was authorised to accept such a resignation under the law.Shafi said he had not received any communication regarding the resignation and that the mayor had also not informed him about it."A resignation has not been received officially. According to Section 40 of the Kerala Municipality Act, the resignation must be submitted to the Secretary. No such resignation letter has been received so far," he said.He said that under the standard procedure, when a councillor or elected representative resigns, the Secretary must immediately report it to the Election Commission."That is what the procedure is. It comes in a specific form. As soon as it is received, an acknowledgement receipt is provided; that is the procedure," he said."Legally, under the Kerala Municipality Act, only the Secretary has the authority to accept a resignation. That doesn't come under the mayor's authority. The act of resignation has not happened here. That is all I can say. As the Secretary, I haven't received an official resignation; only then can I confirm it," he added.Meanwhile, the LDF and its prime constituent, CPIM , are closely watching developments in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, with Left leaders saying they would take an appropriate stand if a governance crisis emerges.The LDF was voted out of power in the corporation last year after ruling it for 45 years.Though Left leaders have not spoken about a possible change in the administration of the state capital's civic body, they said appropriate steps would be taken if the situation arises.If Sreelekha sticks to her decision to resign, the BJP 's strength in the 101-member council will come down to 49.The BJP currently has the support of 51 councillors, including an Independent, while the LDF has 29 councillors and the UDF 20.Speaking to reporters in Palakkad, CPM state secretary MV Govindan said the developments should be viewed as an internal issue within the BJP."As far as we are concerned, there is no other issue. We can think about it only when that time comes," he said.Asked whether the CPM would utilise the situation, he said, "Well, if you ask whether the CPIM will utilise it, how can we not? Do we have any obligation that the BJP must continue running the Corporation when a governance crisis arises? We will take the right stance.""They are people who fall for offers. The fact that not all of them will continue politically is what we are seeing now," he said.
Article Summary: Retired DGP and Bharatiya Janata Party councillor R Sreelekha has reportedly resigned from the Thiruvananthapuram corporation. She was projected as the party's candidate for the post during the 2025 local body elections. The resignation came to light after a message purportedly posted by her in a WhatsApp group of residents.

They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. NEW DELHI: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued and escorted to Gaurikund after a landslide blocked the route late Sunday night, officials said.The pilgrims were stranded around three kilometres from Gaurikund after a landslide hit the route near Chirbasa, news agency ANI reported.The Rudraprayag District Control Room (DCR) informed Sonprayag Police about the situation late on September 27, following which the SDRF Sonprayag team, led by Sub-Inspector Ashish Dimri, rushed to the spot.Prioritising the safety of the pilgrims, the rescue teams carefully assisted them across the affected stretch. Rescue personnel coordinated the movement of pilgrims to ensure they crossed the dangerous stretch safely.The coordinated efforts of the SDRF, NDRF and DDRF helped ensure that all the stranded pilgrims were safely evacuated from the affected area.Officials said the rescue operation was successfully completed despite the challenging conditions at the site.
Article Summary: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.The confrontation took place as the Ujjain Municipal Corporation started removing the mosque portion falling within the proposed road alignment for the widening project ahead of Simhastha 2028.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel are also present at the spot.Earlier, Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav intitaed various develoment works in Ujjain with the demolition activity carried out at his ancestral home.272 structures have been marked for demolition as part of a road-widening project in Ujjain ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.Speaking on the occasion, Yadav said the demolition of his childhood home carried personal significance, but was necessary for the larger cause."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.He added that the gesture was meant to set an example for residents whose properties were also being affected by the project."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation Chairperson Kalawati Yadav explained the scale of preparations underway for the upcoming religious gathering, as it is one of the biggest spiritual gatherings that happens once every 12 years."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. Extensive preparations are underway, including around 29 kilometres of new ghats, a diversion project, dams and other infrastructure works to improve the city. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening initiative forms part of the broader infrastructure overhaul being undertaken in Ujjain to accommodate the massive influx of pilgrims expected during the Simhastha Mela in 2028.
Article Summary: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening project. The situation reportedly turned tense when some unidentified individuals began pelting stones in the area. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.272 structures have been marked for demolition ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.

Article Title: 2,000 cops deployed, classes suspended for 10 days: Lovely Professional University protests spiral into violence - top developments
Article Text:
Rape claim, campus unrest and midnight clashes: What happened at LPU

Police deploy over 2,000 personnel

Clashes, arson and highway blockade

Rape case registered, SIT formed

LPU denies rape claim, releases students' video

Congress attacks Punjab government
